catalog_quote: Das Ur-Ambon betonte alle mehr als einsilbigen Wörter auf der Pänultima des Grundwortes. [...] Eine vierte Gruppe hat den Ton gleichfalls nach dem Wortende zu gerückt, jedoch nur, weil sich dem Stützvokal noch ein weiteres einsilbiges Suffix anheftete. Hierher gehören die Sprachen von Amahei, Nusalaut und Saparua. [...] Die meisten übrigen Abkömmlinge des SA., darunter das Amahei, [...] haben den Akzent auf die nunmehrige Pänultima verschoben, z. B.: Am. rimá-u, rimá-m, rimá-ni. [...] Die Nominalendung -lo, welche sich im Amahei, Saparua und Nusalaut jedem Präfix-Substantivum anheftet, beeinflußt die Lage des Akzentes nicht: Feuer SA. ápu(y) > Am. háu-ro [...] Banane SA. púdi > Am. úsi-ro

new_statements.translation: Proto-Ambon stressed all words of more than one syllable on the penult of the base word. [...] A fourth group has likewise moved the stress towards the end of the word, but only because a further monosyllabic suffix attached itself to the supporting vowel. The languages of Amahei, Nusalaut and Saparua belong here. [...] Most other descendants of SA. [Sub-Ambon], among them Amahei, [...] have shifted the accent onto what is now the penult, e.g. Am. rimá-u, rimá-m, rimá-ni ['my/your/his hand']. [...] The nominal ending -lo, which in Amahei, Saparua and Nusalaut attaches to every prefix-noun, does not affect the position of the accent: fire SA. ápu(y) > Am. háu-ro [...] banana SA. púdi > Am. úsi-ro.

I re-read the saved Google-Books page scan PA174, PA175 and PA177 by eye (and the raw deu scanned of PA175/177/178/179): every sentence in A's quote stands verbatim at the stated pages - p.174 'Das Ur-Ambon betonte alle mehr als einsilbigen Woerter auf der Paenultima des Grundwortes..'; p.175 a) 'Eine vierte Gruppe hat den Ton gleichfalls nach dem Wortende zu gerueckt.. B.: Am. rima-u, rima-m, rima-ni' (acute on -ma-); p.177 e) 'Die Nominalendung -lo, welche sich im Ama…
new_statements.relation_note: Explicit diachronic-synchronic account of accent placement in Amahei within sec. 177; no mention of tone as lexical.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Amahei (Amahai) keeps inherited penultimate stress counted on the word including possessive enclitics (-u, -m, -ni) and the suffix -e (< -ke), which pull stress to the new penult (rimá-ni); the nominal article -ro/-lo and plural -ō are outside the stress domain (háu-ro, úsi-ro, lá'u-ō = surface antepenult), but stress never retreats beyond the antepenult: with two post-stem syllables (-o-lo, -i-ro, -ni-ro) it lands on the antepenult (husúr-o-lo, poó'-i-ro, hurú-nno).
new_statements.exceptions: p.179 g): in rare cases stress jumped one syllable leftward (Am. únjo-lo 'flying fox' < *uníi-lo; ínja-lo 'mountain' < *iní'a-lo); article-bearing nouns surface with antepenultimate stress.
new_statements.identity_note: 'Amahei' = Amahai village language, south Seram (p.2 '13. Amahei (Stres.)', p.13 'Am. = Amahei'); grouped with Nusalaut and Saparua exactly as Collins 1983 / Glottolog Uliase. Our bibliography lists this work twice ('read: silent on stress' with a note that it could not be downloaded, and 'not read: record only'); both tags predate the 2026-09-19 page-image download recorded in the held dir's, so for the catalog it is effectively unread.

sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent or tone; the paper treats the prothetic consonant (h-/y-/w-/zero) in Saparua (Latu), Paulohi, Ruta, Sepa, Tehoru, Asilulu etc. Ruta forms cited without stress marks (ahiro 'hook', aha 'thread', uhano 'cover', aha?uro 'a bamboo'); n.5: 'In Ruta (Amahai) this prothetic h- was perhaps lost at a late date. Stresemann (1927) recorded Amahai hoha'.
